name: clinical_v0_head47_sharp101
rationale: Composed final-layer weights identify units 198 and 38 as positive readout paths that activate for high normalized values. In 128 calibration patients, their active cases remain underestimated after the original affine correction; almost all are measured variables rather than static/administrative channels. Increase only these two effective output coefficients by 1%, a fixed conservative expansion of the existing learned paths. Negative GELU-tail contributions change in the opposite direction, also consistent with the common positive offset in the low/middle range. No fitting, gradients, optimizer or test data. Unit 47 has no positive median-selected activations on the 128-patient calibration cohort. Its negative GELU tail adds positive output with effective coefficient -1.67555; 10300 such scored cases across 127 patients have positive median residual. Sharpen this gate by a fixed conservative 1%: multiply its incoming row and bias by 1.01 and divide its composed outgoing coefficient by 1.01. This preserves the positive linear asymptote and reduces the positive negative-tail contribution. The direct head correction is at most about 0.0049 normalized units; later denoising can propagate it. No fitting, gradient information, optimizer, parameter sweep or test targets determine this explicit edit.
